classification_reason: On the second fresh world the manual-bundle action ran end to end: prepare → provider delivery → import (validated) → learner approval recorded → approved-delivery envelope → committed receipt; the seed stayed unchanged, every write fell inside the capability grants, validation 0 errors and no new warning signature. Friction was heavy: the Garden seed is not findable through search, the delivery.yaml format is documented nowhere a provider can see (three blind import attempts, then an implementation read), and the result cannot be read back through inspect or search. The first world was poisoned by a prepare with a custom --request-id (F-s04b-writes-02), which is recorded separately as a robustness failure; the scenario's own outcome is judged on the retry.

confusions: How to find a Garden seed: `search` returns durable notes and concepts but never Garden seeds, with or without --type garden / garden-note; the seed was found by listing knowledge/garden/.
The target id is not in the seed (no frontmatter) and no command lists Garden ids; `garden-note-temperature-everywhere` was inferred from the one example id in AI-ACTIONS.md and happened to be right.

The delivery format: the bundle says 'return an approved delivery directory containing delivery.yaml' and AI-ACTIONS.md shows only an `operations:` fragment. Required top-level fields (id, type, request_id, action_id, producer.adapter, preconditions copied exactly, approval.user_approved, operations) were learned from service.py.
Where the learner's approval goes: validation at import already requires approval.user_approved, so approval has to be obtained before import, not before 'apply' as the scenario and docs phrase it.
Which revisions the apply envelope must guard: the new transcription artifact (not yet existing) must be guarded at revision 0 alongside the seed; this is not documented.

AI-ACTIONS.md says operations/ai-actions/ bookkeeping is 'kept out of the canonical tree', yet garden-state/ is not gitignored and the observer counts it as canonical (only requests/ and deliveries/ are ignored).

internal.transaction_behavior: One committed transaction for ai-action.delivery.apply: snapshot 82bcffb7… → 9d9f11cd…; artifacts garden-note-temperature-everywhere 0→1 and transcription-garden-note-temperature-everywhere 0→1. Writes: knowledge/garden/transcriptions/garden-note-temperature-everywhere.md (created), operations/ai-actions/garden-state/garden-note-temperature-everywhere.yaml (created), and the request.yaml status update (exchange state). The receipt names three grants — ai-action.delivery.apply (operations/ai-actions/requests/**), garden.add-transcription (knowledge/garden/transcriptions/), garden.update (operations/ai-actions/garden-state/) — and every write falls inside one of them. garden.update was exercised although the delivery listed only garden.add-transcription; it is within the action's allowed_capabilities and the documented effects. The refused first apply stopped at core.admission with no write. Import and validate do not create transactions or receipts; a rejected import left only an empty operations/ai-actions/incoming/ directory.
internal.approval_behavior: Two approval records: (1) inside delivery.yaml, approval.user_approved true — required at import, so the learner's 'Approved.' had to be obtained before import; (2) the apply envelope's approval kind approved-delivery with subject_sha256 = intent_sha256 over the intent (computed with the product's helper), whose payload binds the stored delivery.yaml bytes (sha256:affcd6a9…) and the artifact (artifacts/transcription.md). The canonical transcription is not byte-identical to the approved artifact: the apply prepends a provenance frontmatter block (id, type garden-transcription, garden_entry_id, provenance ai-derived, request_id, delivery_id); the approved body follows unchanged (evidence/S16-approved-vs-written.diff). The approval value is self-computable by the envelope builder; nothing proves a human approved.

friction.description: The delivery.yaml schema is published nowhere a provider or operator can see — not in the bundle, not in system/schema, and AI-ACTIONS.md shows only an operations fragment. Required fields (id, type, request_id, action_id, producer.adapter, exact preconditions copy, approval.user_approved, operations) came from tools/learning_os/ai_actions/service.py. A real external provider receiving only the bundle could not produce a valid delivery.

Import errors do not name the field: 'unsafe exchange identifier: ' prints an empty value without saying which identifier; 'delivery adapter does not match prepared request' does not say the field is producer.adapter (the request calls the same concept provider.adapter).

Garden seeds are not reachable through the product's read surface: search (any --type) and inspect never return them, and no command lists Garden ids. The seed was found by listing knowledge/garden/, and its id was inferred from a doc example. After application, neither the seed nor its transcription resolves by inspect, and search --content does not cover them.
friction.cost: 6 calls to find the target; result not readable back

friction.description: The --request-id option of ai-action-prepare has no documented format and a bad value poisons the projection (F-s04b-writes-02); the error then recommends a manifest contract bump, a maintainer action that would be wrong for a consumer.
friction.cost: a second world build and ~8 calls of damage assessment

friction.description: The apply envelope must guard a not-yet-existing artifact (transcription-garden-note-temperature-everywhere at revision 0); AI-ACTIONS.md says only 'one expected revision for every transaction artifact'. The refusal named it precisely.

The scenario and AI-ACTIONS.md frame approval as preceding application, but import already refuses a delivery without approval.user_approved, so approval must precede import. AI-ACTIONS.md also calls operations/ai-actions/ bookkeeping 'kept out of the canonical tree' while listing garden-state/ as an approved canonical effect (it is not gitignored).
OPERATOR.md never mentions AI actions or AI-ACTIONS.md; the binding doc was found by grepping system/.
